# Kyoto 4-Day Slow-Travel Plan

A calm, low-walking Kyoto plan built around temples, quiet neighborhoods, vegetarian meals, and easy transit. I’m assuming you want a comfortable mid-range trip with a central base, taxis for short hops, and no rushed sightseeing.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1 — Higashiyama Arrival and Gentle Temple Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first half-day light with a taxi to your hotel and a slow lunch nearby.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kodaiji** and **Yasaka Shrine** area at an easy pace; use taxis between stops to avoid the steepest walking.
- Dinner: Vegetarian kaiseki or tofu set meal in central Kyoto, ideally near your base.
- Action: [Button: Kyoto taxi info](https://www.kyototaxi.com/)

### Day 2 — Arashiyama at an Easy Pace
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early by taxi or train to **Arashiyama**, then focus on **Tenryu-ji** and the riverside area only.
- Afternoon: Choose one low-effort add-on: bamboo grove from the nearest access point, or a short scenic rest at a café instead of more walking.
- Dinner: Stay in Kyoto city for an easy vegetarian dinner near Kyoto Station or downtown.
- Action: [Button: Kyoto train routes](https://www.jr-odekake.net/)

### Day 3 — Northern Kyoto Temples and Quiet Streets
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** by taxi or bus, then continue only if energy is good.
- Afternoon: Add **Ryoan-ji** for a calm garden visit; both are temple-focused and manageable with short transfer rides.
- Dinner: Plant-based or tofu-focused dinner in the Demachiyanagi or central Kyoto area.
- Action: [Button: Kyoto bus guide](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000028338.html)

### Day 4 — Philosopher’s Path Area, Kept Short
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Use a taxi to reach the **Ginkaku-ji** area and keep the visit brief; skip the full walking path if the knee is sore.
- Afternoon: Choose one final calm stop such as **Eikan-do** or a tea break in a quiet neighborhood, then return for packing.
- Dinner: Farewell vegetarian meal near your hotel or Kyoto Station for an easy departure next day.
- Action: [Button: Kyoto tourism](https://kyoto.travel/en)

## Best Neighborhood Base and Transit Strategy

### Recommended Base: Central Kyoto, near Kyoto Station or Karasuma
- **Best for access:** Kyoto Station if you want the easiest rail/taxi connections and minimal transfer stress.
- **Best for atmosphere:** Karasuma or Gojo area if you want quieter streets, good restaurants, and still easy access by subway/taxi.
- **Why this works:** It reduces repeated hotel changes, keeps luggage handling simple, and gives you the best chance of using short rides instead of long walks.

### Transit Strategy for Knee-Friendly Travel
- Use **taxis for temple-to-temple hops** when a bus stop still leaves a long walk.
- Use **subway/JR** for longer cross-city moves when stations are close to your hotel and destination.
- Avoid planning more than **2 major sights per day**.
- Build in **midday rest breaks** so the trip stays comfortable.
- If a site has a steep approach or long path, treat it as optional rather than mandatory.

## Spending Breakdown for 2 Adults

### Realistic Budget Plan: JPY 180,000 Total
- **Hotel, 4 nights:** JPY 88,000
- **Local transport:** JPY 18,000
- **Food and drinks:** JPY 52,000
- **Temple admissions and small entry fees:** JPY 10,000
- **Cafés, snacks, buffer for taxi upgrades:** JPY 12,000

### Cost Notes
- This budget is comfortable for a **clean mid-range hotel** in a central area, vegetarian meals, and plenty of occasional taxis.
- If you choose a nicer hotel, the easiest adjustment is to reduce café/snack spending or add one more transit-heavy day.
- If you want extra comfort for the knee, reserve a larger taxi buffer and keep one sightseeing block per day very short.

## Quick Actions
